_readme: Documentation, NOT an argument to confluence_create_page. Pass space_key, title, parent_id and content. Before creating the page, replace the literal token {{MERGE_COMMIT}} in the first panel with the squash-merge SHA on main. That token is the only placeholder in this file, and grep finds it TWICE: once in the panel, which is the one to replace, and once in the sentence above, which is this _readme naming it. _readme is not passed to the create call, so a global substitution is harmless -- but a verifying grep should expect 2, not 1.

artefacts and asserts this file carries that value. It proves

The §2 row exists because it once did not.
The headline sentences are the ones most likely to be copied out alone, so they are what a transcription guarantee most needs to cover; at
they were the one thing it did not cover, and changing

rather than against the report as a whole, so a needle satisfied by some other paragraph cannot stand in for them.
The §6 and §8 rows exist for the same reason, one round later.
§6's root-cause row was published as a zero, on the stated ground that no committed artefact carried the check-name sheet. That was wrong about a committed artefact:
. So the names and the counts are asserted — each name in the R1–R6 table is parsed out of
and looked up in that list, each parenthetical is asserted against the number of names beside it, and R2's
is asserted against the failing checks whose own message states an HTTP status. §8 had no row at all while the table was published as complete.
What is not checked, and it is one thing: the attribution.
root cause a given failing check belongs to is a reading of the run directory, which is
— only the censuses are — so no assertion here could be made to fail on a wrong grouping. S5-30's
is a figure of that same kind: it counts how many failing checks the census's
prose accounts for, which is a property of the grouping and not of the census's numbers.
A Sprint 6 planner should treat the grouping as an argument to verify against the run, and the names and counts as transcribed.
One more bound, on the check that guards the mirror.
The Confluence payload is compared to this file token by token, so a rendering that drops, reorders or invents a sentence fails. It proves the two copies
passes it. It is a divergence check, not a second opinion, and the transcription check above is what makes the shared value right in the first place.
